title: PuTR-CouT: Counting-by-Tracking in Camera-Trap Image Sequences
abstract: Species identification in camera trap images has been widely studied, but key ecological modeling tasks such as species abundance or density estimation also require counting individual animals. However, the lack of counting labels in most datasets and low frame rates (typically ~1 frame per second) make sequence-level tracking and count estimation particularly challenging. In this work, we present PuTR-CouT, a counting-by-tracking framework built on a transformer-based learned association mechanism for sequence-level animal counting in camera trap images. To address the scarcity of annotated tracking data, we generate synthetic training data by exploiting structural priors, such as static backgrounds and short temporal bursts, to heuristically create pseudo-tracking labels in a weakly supervised manner. The resulting tracker associates detections across frames, using these tracks to estimate per-species counts. We also refine the MaxBoxCount heuristic used by the top solutions of the iWildCam 2021 challenge as a strong baseline, setting the highest score reported to date. When evaluated on the iWildCam 2021 benchmark, our framework PuTR-CouT delivers competitive counting results compared to the improved MaxBoxCount, with the added capability of multi-species predictions and track-level verification.

title: Multi-Fidelity Gaussian Processes for Translational Modelling of Clinical Outcomes
abstract: Bridging the gap between animal and human experiments remains a major challenge in translational medicine, particularly in early drug development. Progress is constrained by financial cost, the difficulty of integrating heterogeneous in vitro and in vivo data, and the desire to reduce the use of animal testing balanced against minimising the risk to human participants. We present a statistical machine learning framework using multi-fidelity Gaussian processes, in which animal studies are considered as lower fidelity but informative approximations to human experiments. This allows cross-species similarities and nonlinear exposure-response relationships to be learned simultaneously, enabling principled extrapolation between species while quantifying uncertainty. By leveraging information from multiple experimental fidelities, our method improves estimation of clinically relevant quantities of interest and supports the replacement, reduction, and refinement of in vivo testing. We first illustrate this approach in a simulated scenario, before validating it on real clinical data. We simulate data for drug-induced QT-interval prolongation, a key cardiac safety assessment required for regulatory approval. This framework provides a probabilistic surrogate capable of integrating in vitro pharmacology, animal experiments and human data within a unified statistical model. Crucially, it achieves this at no additional experimental cost while also enabling transfer learning across compounds. As a result, predictions and uncertainty quantification for new drugs can be generated from in vitro findings alone, providing additional efficiency gains and accelerating decision making. For validation, we use a clinical dataset measuring change in heart rate under autonomic blockade, which represents some of the challenges commonly found in multi-species datasets.

title: ProtLingo: Efficient Protein Language Modeling via Conditional Memory and Expert Routing
abstract: Proteins perform diverse cellular functions, and even single amino-acid substitutions can alter stability, activity, or molecular interactions. Protein language models (PLMs) provide a scalable approach for modeling such sequence--function relationships from unlabeled sequences, but increasing the size of dense Transformer backbones often brings substantial computational cost without consistently improving mutation-sensitive prediction. We introduce ProtLingo, an efficient PLM framework that augments a pretrained single-sequence backbone with conditional local memory and sparse expert routing. ProtLingo maps contextual residue representations into route-specific discrete codes, composes centered local windows into latent $N$-gram addresses, and retrieves reusable residual signals associated with recurring local sequence contexts. In parallel, selected feed-forward blocks are upcycled into sparse Mixture-of-Experts layers with shared and routed experts, enabling residue-dependent computation while activating only a subset of parameters. Experiments on protein fitness prediction, FLIP benchmarks, and supervised contact prediction show that ProtLingo achieves competitive performance with a 150M-scale backbone, including strong parameter efficiency on mutation-effect prediction and preserved long-range structural representations.

title: Shapley Valuation of Finite-Copy Quantum Data Depends on Physical Access
abstract: Data valuation asks how learning utility should be attributed to training data contributors. Most classical formulations begin after data have become reusable records, so the physical readout of the data is effectively fixed. Finite-copy quantum data are different: unknown states are consumable physical systems, and the same supplied states and downstream task can yield different Shapley values under different physical access models. Our framework makes this dependence explicit by treating physical access as a component of quantum data valuation itself. We establish an exact connection between physical-access advantage and contributor-level data valuation. For nested access models, we prove that the maximal downstream utility gain enabled by richer physical access exactly determines the largest symmetric Shapley ranking-reversal margin. More generally, for arbitrary access-model pairs, including non-nested ones, we derive an exact geometric characterization of the possible shifts of the full Shapley attribution vector. For fixed learning pipelines, we further obtain an operational Shapley-observable representation for finite-copy valuation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that identical quantum samples can receive different values and rankings when only the physical access model is changed. These results establish that quantum data value is not an intrinsic property of the underlying states alone, but emerges from the interaction between quantum states, physical access, and the downstream learning task.

title: The Bracket and the Bootstrap: Quantum Machine Learning, Classical Econometrics, and the Measurement of AI Governance Readiness.
abstract: This book examines a specific methodological gap: the absence of a benchmarking comparison between quantum machine learning (QML) and classical econometric methods applied to the problem of measuring and explaining AI governance readiness — a comparison already conducted in finance and, more distantly, in climate science, but not yet in this field. Building from foundational quantum formalism and the current econometric toolkit used in AI governance research, the book traces the genealogy of quantum econometrics from mathematical analogy to applied benchmarking, then runs an illustrative case study comparing a bootstrap mediation pipeline against a quantum-kernel regression on a 23-country synthetic dataset structured to mirror real cross-national governance data. It concludes that classical econometrics currently retains a demonstrated advantage for this specific research problem, and proposes a concrete, conditional research agenda for revisiting the comparison as AI-governance data matures.

title: 基于异质拓扑的动态信息编码算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic information encoding algorithm based on the principles of heterogeneous topology. Traditional information compression techniques often focus solely on the data itself, failing to fully exploit the inherent structural properties of the information. This work proposes a new approach that leverages the geometric structures inherent within the data to optimize both compression and transmission efficiency. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating a dynamic topology, allowing the algorithm to adaptively adjust encoding parameters based on the information's characteristics. This dynamic adjustment enables significant improvements in information compression ratios and transmission reliability compared to existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in various data types.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution Protocols Based on Chaotic Bit Synchronization
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a revolutionary paradigm shift in secure communication, offering unprecedented levels of security based on the laws of physics. However, current QKD protocols face challenges related to key generation and distribution, particularly in the face of environmental noise and imperfect synchronization. This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol, termed "Chaotic Bit Synchronization" (CBS), designed to mitigate these challenges by dynamically adjusting key parameters based on the rate of change in the bit synchronization. This dynamic adaptation significantly enhances key quality and robustness, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable QKD systems. The core mechanism centers around the implementation of a 'chaotic bit synchronization' metric, continuously adjusting key parameters to maintain a stable, high-quality key. This paper provides a detailed analysis of the CBS protocol, exploring its mathematical foundations, operational characteristics, and potential advantages over existing approaches.

title: Chaos Domain Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Chaos Domain Quantum Algorithm (CDQA), designed to efficiently search for optimal solutions within complex systems and predict their dynamic behavior. The CDQA leverages the unique properties of chaotic domains to accelerate the identification of potential solutions, offering a significant advancement over existing optimization techniques. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in a specific, challenging scenario. The core mechanism hinges on the manipulation of quantum states within a chaotic domain, allowing for the exploration of a vast solution space with enhanced computational efficiency.

title: Adaptive Self-Stiffness Framework
abstract: The present work introduces an Adaptive Self-Stiffness Framework designed to enhance the generalization and stability of machine learning models. Traditional approaches often rely solely on model architecture, limiting the potential for improvement. This framework proposes a novel mechanism for dynamically adjusting model parameters, effectively promoting self-regulation and robustness within the model. The core concept revolves around a self-regulating 'stiffness' parameter, which influences the model's internal structure and behavior. This approach aims to overcome limitations of existing techniques, offering a fundamentally new way to improve model performance.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Complex System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel neuro-symbolic reasoning framework designed for modeling complex system dynamics. The core principle centers on integrating neural network-based pattern recognition with symbolic reasoning to facilitate efficient modeling, prediction, and explanation of intricate multi-agent systems. Current approaches often fall short in handling the inherent complexity and ambiguity of these systems, necessitating a more robust and flexible approach. This research investigates a hybrid architecture that leverages the strengths of both neural networks and symbolic systems, aiming to provide a superior model of dynamic behavior. The work will detail the integration of neural networks for rapid pattern identification and symbolic reasoning for inference and explanation. This framework will be presented through a detailed conceptual overview, outlining the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation metrics. We will specifically address the challenges of scaling and maintaining representational fidelity across diverse system configurations.

title: 基于非对称矩阵的自适应量子算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and cryptography. However, achieving practical quantum advantage requires efficient quantum algorithms and robust quantum hardware. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization based on non-symmetric matrix transformations. We propose a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism leveraging quantum entanglement, specifically termed "quantum pulses," to automatically tailor quantum algorithm parameters based on the input data's characteristics. The core mechanism involves manipulating the quantum state through the entanglement of quantum states to achieve a more efficient and targeted quantum computation. This approach addresses a critical limitation of current quantum algorithms – the reliance on predefined, static parameter adjustments – and promises significant improvements in algorithm performance, particularly for complex data sets. The paper details the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this method. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this technology.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Modular Geometry (DAM)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamically Adaptive Modular Geometry (DAM), a novel framework for geometric modeling that dynamically adjusts geometric primitives and constraints based on real-time data analysis. DAM leverages a self-correcting neural network to optimize geometric parameters, enhancing the robustness and adaptability of computational models. The core mechanism centers around a "geometry-aware neural network" that learns to adjust parameters in response to observed data, eliminating the need for pre-defined rules and fostering a fundamentally new approach to modeling. We detail the system architecture, demonstrate its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discuss its potential impact across various scientific and engineering domains.

title: Graph Neural Network-Based Software Architecture Design Method
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for software architecture design based on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The core idea is to leverage the power of GNNs to learn the structural characteristics of software architectures and automatically generate design solutions. Existing software architecture design methods often rely heavily on manual effort and expert knowledge. This approach offers a more automated and potentially more efficient way to design complex software systems. We represent a software architecture as a graph, where nodes represent components and edges represent relationships between them. A GNN is then trained on this graph to learn patterns and dependencies. Finally, the learned GNN is utilized to predict and generate new architectural designs. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline key considerations for implementation. This research contributes to the field of software architecture design by exploring the application of GNNs, opening possibilities for automated design and potentially improved system quality.

title: Fractal Dimension-Based Error Correction in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal dimension metrics to enhance error correction within neural networks, aiming to mitigate instability and improve model performance. Traditional error metrics often fail to capture the complex dynamics of error propagation, leading to suboptimal network behavior. We introduce a novel fractal dimension metric that mimics the self-similarity observed in many neural network errors, allowing for proactive weight adjustment. This approach offers a more robust and adaptive mechanism for error management, potentially addressing key challenges in neural network design and training. The core mechanism involves quantifying the error's fractal dimension, which is then used to dynamically adjust the network's weights, thereby minimizing errors. This paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments, showcasing improved stability and accuracy compared to conventional error correction techniques.

title: Meta-Learning for Algorithm Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging the principles of meta-learning. Traditional algorithm optimization often relies on manual tuning or evolutionary algorithms, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield optimal results. Our method addresses this limitation by utilizing a meta-learning model to learn adaptive optimization strategies directly from data. The core idea involves training a meta-learner to effectively adjust algorithm parameters and potentially even their underlying structure. We explore both model-based meta-learning and reinforcement learning approaches to achieve this adaptive optimization. The proposed framework offers a dynamic and potentially more efficient solution compared to conventional optimization techniques, leading to improved performance across a range of algorithmic problems. We outline the key components, including the meta-learner architecture, the learning process, and the adaptation mechanisms, and provide a conceptual overview of its implementation.

title: Ảnh hưởng của khả năng Chatbot Artificial Intelligence (Chatbot AI) đến sự gắn kết của khách hàng trong dịch vụ trực tuyến
abstract: Nghiên cứu phân tích ảnh hưởng của khả năng hệ thống hội thoại tự động ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (Chatbot AI) đến sự gắn kết của khách hàng trong dịch vụ trực tuyến tại Việt Nam. Dựa trên lý thuyết phản ứng xã hội (SRT), nghiên cứu kiểm định mô hình gồm khả năng sử dụng, khả năng phản hồi, năng lực được nhận thức, sự chân thực được nhận thức và sự gắn kết của khách hàng. Dữ liệu từ 488 người dùng đã tương tác với Chatbot AI được phân tích bằng mô hình cấu trúc dựa trên bình phương nhỏ nhất từng phần (PLS-SEM). Kết quả cho thấy khả năng sử dụng và khả năng phản hồi tác động tích cực đến năng lực được nhận thức; năng lực được nhận thức tác động tích cực đến sự chân thực được nhận thức và sự gắn kết của khách hàng; đồng thời sự chân thực được nhận thức thúc đẩy sự gắn kết của khách hàng. Kết quả gợi ý doanh nghiệp dịch vụ trực tuyến cần thiết kế Chatbot AI dễ sử dụng, phản hồi phù hợp và tạo cảm giác có năng lực, chân thực nhằm nâng cao sự gắn kết của khách hàng.

title: Large Language Models for Heterogeneous Data Mining in Liver Disease: Framework Development and Retrospective Validation Study
abstract: Abstract Background Differentiating among liver disease entities such as autoimmune liver disease (AILD), drug-induced liver injury (DILI), and chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains clinically challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and nonspecific laboratory findings. Conventional machine learning (ML) approaches rely mainly on structured laboratory data, whereas free-text clinical reports and other heterogeneous electronic medical record data are often underused. Large language models (LLMs) may provide a strategy for encoding heterogeneous clinical information, yet their usefulness for liver disease classification remains insufficiently evaluated. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the usefulness of LLM-derived embeddings for clinical data mining in liver disease and to determine whether integrating these embeddings with laboratory variables improves classification across broad disease categories and closely related subtypes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed electronic medical record data from 7543 patients with nonoverlapping liver disease etiologies treated at Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between 2010 and 2025. Three LLMs (Qwen3, Huatuo-o1, and II-Medical) generated semantic embeddings from standardized clinical text, combining free-text examination reports, and structured clinical observations. Performance was assessed in a 3-class etiological task (AILD, DILI, and CHB) and a 4-class task further subclassifying AILD into autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis. We compared embedding-only models, LLM-integrated ML models, and an ML-only baseline using the same structured variable set and preprocessing pipeline, with lightweight natural language processing encoders and zero-shot LLM reasoning as additional comparators. Models were developed using 5-fold cross-validation and evaluated on an internal holdout set using accuracy, macroaveraged precision, recall, and F 1 -score. Results In the 3-class task, the LLM-integrated ML models achieved macro F 1 -scores of 0.835‐0.837, compared with 0.791 for the ML-only baseline, with corresponding accuracies of 0.925‐0.929 versus 0.893. In the 4-class task, the LLM-integrated ML models achieved macro F 1 -scores of 0.717‐0.734, compared with 0.665 for the ML-only baseline, with corresponding accuracies of 0.920‐0.922 versus 0.874. A temporal split sensitivity analysis using cases from 2010 to 2019 for training and cases from 2020 to 2025 for testing showed that the relative advantage of LLM-integrated ML models over the ML-only baseline was preserved. Direct zero-shot LLM reasoning and lightweight natural language processing encoders performed below the embedding-based integrated models. Conclusions In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with clear-cut, nonoverlapping liver disease etiologies, LLM-derived embeddings provided complementary information to structured laboratory variables for multiclass liver disease classification. The integrated framework showed improved internal validation performance compared with the ML-only model, particularly for non-CHB categories and fine-grained subtype discrimination. Because patients with overlapping liver disease etiologies were excluded, the reported performance may overestimate diagnostic accuracy in broader real-world clinical settings where overlapping syndromes are common. Multicenter external validation and prospective evaluation in more heterogeneous patient populations are needed before clinical implementation.

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Heterogeneous Data Mining in Liver Disease: Framework Development and Retrospective Validation Study
evidence.abstract: Abstract Background Differentiating among liver disease entities such as autoimmune liver disease (AILD), drug-induced liver injury (DILI), and chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains clinically challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and nonspecific laboratory findings. Conventional machine learning (ML) approaches rely mainly on structured laboratory data, whereas free-text clinical reports and other heterogeneous electronic medical record data are often underused. Large language models (LLMs) may provide a strategy for encoding heterogeneous clinical information, yet their usefulness for liver disease classification remains insufficiently evaluated. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the usefulness of LLM-derived embeddings for clinical data mining in liver disease and to determine whether integrating these embeddings with laboratory variables improves classification across broad disease categories and closely related subtypes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed electronic medical record data from 7543 patients with nonoverlapping liver disease etiologies treated at Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between 2010 and 2025. Three LLMs (Qwen3, Huatuo-o1, and II-Medical) generated semantic embeddings from standardized clinical text, combining free-text examination reports, and structured clinical observations. Performance was assessed in a 3-class etiological task (AILD, DILI, and CHB) and a 4-class task further subclassifying AILD into autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis. We compared embedding-only models, LLM-integrated ML models, and an ML-only baseline using the same structured variable set and preprocessing pipeline, with lightweight natural language processing encoders and zero-shot LLM reasoning as additional comparators. Models were developed using 5-fold cross-validation and evaluated on an internal holdout set using accuracy, macroaveraged precision, recall, and F 1 -score. Results In the 3-class task, the LLM-integrated ML models achieved macro F 1 -scores of 0.835‐0.837, compared with 0.791 for the ML-only baseline, with corresponding accuracies of 0.925‐0.929 versus 0.893. In the 4-class task, the LLM-integrated ML models achieved macro F 1 -scores of 0.717‐0.734, compared with 0.665 for the ML-only baseline, with corresponding accuracies of 0.920‐0.922 versus 0.874. A temporal split sensitivity analysis using cases from 2010 to 2019 for training and cases from 2020 to 2025 for testing showed that the relative advantage of LLM-integrated ML models over the ML-only baseline was preserved. Direct zero-shot LLM reasoning and lightweight natural language processing encoders performed below the embedding-based integrated models. Conclusions In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with clear-cut, nonoverlapping liver disease etiologies, LLM-derived embeddings provided complementary information to structured laboratory variables for multiclass liver disease classification. The integrated framework showed improved internal validation performance compared with the ML-only model, particularly for non-CHB categories and fine-grained subtype discrimination. Because patients with overlapping liver disease etiologies were excluded, the reported performance may overestimate diagnostic accuracy in broader real-world clinical settings where overlapping syndromes are common. Multicenter external validation and prospective evaluation in more heterogeneous patient populations are needed before clinical implementation.

abstract: "This dataset contains annotated English\u2013Hindi code-mixed YouTube comments developed for research on the data annotation task. The dataset can be used to develop, evaluate, and compare machine learning and deep learning approaches for bullying detection in multilingual and code-mixed environments."

title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence model for basal cell carcinoma detection and section completeness assessment in Mohs micrographic surgery in an Asian cohort
abstract: Background: Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma (BCC) requires rapid intraoperative histologic interpretation. This is labor-intensive and incomplete tissue sections compromise margin assessment. Artificial intelligence has shown promise in BCC detection but section completeness assessment remains underexplored. Objective: Develop and validate an artificial intelligence model for BCC detection and section completeness assessment on Mohs frozen-section histology. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study using histology slides from 130 patients who underwent Mohs surgery for BCC from 2017 to 2025. Whole slides were digitized and annotated. A convolutional neural network model was trained to detect BCC and classify section completeness. Model performance assessment with standard performance metrics and region-of-interest evaluation was performed. Results: The BCC detection model achieved accuracy 0.993, sensitivity 0.915, specificity 0.996, precision 0.889, F1-score 0.902 at the tile level, with comparable region-of-interest sensitivity (0.910). The section completeness model achieved accuracy 0.890, sensitivity 0.948, specificity 0.524, precision 0.927, and F1-score 0.937. Limitations: Single-center retrospective design, limited representation of rare BCC subtypes, and no direct comparison with human experts. Conclusion: Although the specificity for section completeness was low, further research and additional model training may enable development of a model with improved performance.

title: Learning Spatial-Spectral Refinement and Calibrating Complementary Observations for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HMIF) aims to reconstruct a high-resolution hyperspectral image (HR-HSI) by combining the fine spatial details of a high-resolution multispectral image (HR-MSI) with the rich spectral information of a low-resolution hyperspectral image (LR-HSI). Recent advances in implicit neural representations (INRs) have enabled flexible coordinate-based modeling for HMIF; however, existing INR-based approaches may not fully capture fine-grained spatial structures and rich spectral dependencies. Moreover, the LR-HSI and HR-MSI are primarily incorporated through degradation-consistency constraints, leaving their complementary information underexploited. To address these limitations, we propose Two-Stage Reconstruction with Implicit Tensor Neural Representation (TSR-ITNR), a unified self-supervised framework integrating representation refinement and observation-guided calibration. In Stage 1, TSR-ITNR learns an implicit Tucker representation and refines its low-rank spatial coefficient tensor and spectral basis to better capture fine spatial structures and interband correlations. A fixed pretrained denoiser further provides a deep prior for the preliminary reconstruction. In Stage 2, parameter-free calibration derives complementary and noninterfering corrections from both observations to recover information insufficiently captured in Stage 1. Theoretical analysis establishes the geometry-preserving property of spectral refinement and the orthogonal complementarity of calibration. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate strong quantitative, visual, and spectral reconstruction performance without ground-truth HR-HSI supervision. Beyond conventional reconstruction metrics, we further assess the effectiveness of TSR-ITNR using downstream semantic segmentation accuracy.

title: How do LLMs Evaluate Perceived Moral Agency? Investigating Moral Decision-Making in Human-Artificial Agents Interactions
abstract: As LLMs take on roles requiring moral advice, understanding how they attribute moral agency becomes critical. Humans possess moral agency, the capacity to make ethically guided decisions and bear responsibility for their consequences, a well-established construct in moral psychology. Yet as artificial agents (AAs) such as robots, drones, and disembodied AI systems become increasingly embedded in smart city environments, the question of whether and how moral agency is attributed to them takes on new urgency. This paper presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first empirical study comparing how humans and LLMs evaluate perceived moral agency (PMA) across human and autonomous artificial agents varying in embodiment, situated in plausible smart city scenarios. Using an adaptation of a validated PMA scale, we applied a protocol to 190 human participants as well as various LLMs. Our evaluation reveals higher perceptions of moral agency in humans than in AAs. However, when facing moral dilemmas in concrete scenarios, LLMs reason outward from the situation, prioritizing harm severity and contextual urgency over any stable assessment of the agent itself, amplifying a context-sensitivity also present in human raters. These findings are particularly relevant as LLMs become increasingly involved in everyday moral decisions.

title: Mask Noise Robustness in Time-Delay Reservoir Computing System
abstract: 随着延时型储备池计算（Time-delay reservoir computing, TDRC）相关技术的成熟，全硬件集成成为主流发展方向，硬件生成掩码时将不可避免引入噪声。掩码信号作为输入层时间复用与高维状态编码的重要部分，其噪声的存在会直接破坏固定的输入映射权重，影响系统的计算性能。本文将高斯白噪声融入掩码信号，对比研究了数字掩码（二值、六值）与模拟掩码（混沌）在不同强度噪声下TDRC的性能表现。结果表明，使用数字二值掩码的系统最高可容忍信噪比7.539 dB的强掩码噪声，其噪声容忍度远大于模拟混沌掩码（约18dB）。同时发现，掩码波形的拓扑复杂度对系统抗噪能力也有关键影响，即使在同类型掩码下，不同波形模式的系统掩码噪声容忍度最大可差10.8 dB。结合非线性动力学开展机理剖析，阐明该性能差异的内在物理成因，为未来延时型储备池计算系统的全硬件集成提供了重要指导。

title: Probability Logic Dynamic Matrix Formula
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic logic-based matrix formula designed for efficient computation and optimization, particularly within the realms of machine learning and optimization problems. The core mechanism leverages a dynamic adjustment mechanism embedded within the matrix formula itself, allowing for automatic parameter variation and model refinement. Traditional matrix approaches often require a one-time adjustment, hindering their adaptability to evolving data. This work proposes a method that dynamically adapts the matrix's parameters based on the input data, improving performance and robustness. The formula's design incorporates a layered approach that combines probabilistic reasoning with matrix operations, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Probability Density Estimation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probability density estimation leveraging quantum entanglement. We propose a method wherein entangled particles are utilized to create a correlated probabilistic field, effectively acting as a quantum sensor. This sensor allows for the calculation of highly accurate probabilities with a dramatically reduced computational cost compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism centers around establishing a strong correlation between the entangled particles, allowing for the quantification of complex probability distributions with unparalleled precision. The resulting system offers a significant advantage in terms of efficiency and accuracy, potentially revolutionizing probabilistic modeling across various fields. The paper details the theoretical framework, experimental setup, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this quantum-enhanced approach.

title: 拓扑动力学信息论
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological dynamics to information theory, focusing on the development of a novel algorithmic approach for quantum information processing. The core claim centers on the creation of a "topological quantum entanglement" mechanism, which leverages the inherent non-linearity of topological structures to enhance the efficiency of information encoding and processing. Traditional topological dynamics has primarily been applied to fields such as materials science and bioinformatics, lacking a foundational framework for quantum computation and information handling. This work proposes a new methodology that integrates topological principles with information theory, aiming to provide a powerful tool for the design and implementation of quantum information processing systems. The paper details the core mechanism, highlights its potential advantages, and discusses future research directions.

title: 基于自适应的量子态的非线性拓扑变换
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum state manipulation utilizing adaptive topology transformations. Traditional methods often rely on predefined transformation rules, while this work introduces a dynamic topology transformation that enables precise control over quantum states. We explore the design and implementation of a system capable of predicting the stability of quantum states and achieving precise manipulation through this adaptive framework. The core mechanism centers around the continuous adjustment of a quantum state based on a defined transformation, allowing for dynamic shifts and manipulations that surpass the limitations of traditional methods. This research contributes to a fundamentally new paradigm in quantum state evolution and control.

The core mechanism focuses on manipulating the inherent structure of the Hilbert space to facilitate faster and more accurate computations. This work represents a significant step towards developing quantum algorithms with enhanced capabilities and adaptability.

title: Dynamic Multi-Particle Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a novel dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm for quantum systems, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, limiting precision and efficiency. Our approach utilizes machine learning to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters, offering a significant advancement in modeling and control, particularly within the realms of quantum computing and quantum communication. The core mechanism centers around learning and automated parameter optimization based on a carefully designed feedback loop. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations and theoretical analysis, showcasing its potential to achieve accurate and efficient modeling of complex quantum systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Classical Geometry: A Computational Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, possesses unique properties that offer the potential for transformative computational capabilities. This paper explores the application of entangled states to construct a novel computational framework, leveraging entanglement for instantaneous information transfer and synchronization. We propose a model that transforms entanglement into a geometric structure, enabling near-instantaneous data synchronization, and investigate its potential within distributed computation. The core claim centers on the realization of instantaneous data exchange and synchronization through the exploitation of entanglement's inherent properties. This work suggests a significant departure from traditional algorithmic approaches, offering a potential pathway for large-scale distributed computation with enhanced efficiency.

title: 自适应量子势场计算的机器学习辅助
abstract: This paper explores the integration of machine learning techniques into the process of quantum state field (QSF) calculation. Traditional QSF calculation relies heavily on computationally intensive algorithms, often limiting the complexity of quantum systems that can be studied. We propose a system leveraging a machine learning model to predict QSF, enabling automated parameter adjustment and ultimately, increased computational efficiency and precision. This approach addresses a critical limitation of existing methods by providing a dynamic and adaptive strategy. The core of this work involves training a model to emulate the quantum system's behavior, allowing for a shift towards more streamlined and effective calculations. The research demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in both computational speed and accuracy through the strategic application of machine learning.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive geometric algorithm based on quantum topology, designed to precisely model and compute complex geometric shapes. Traditional geometric algorithms often rely on static representations, limiting their ability to effectively handle intricate geometries. This algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum topology – a theoretical framework that describes geometric structures through entanglement and superposition – to dynamically adjust geometric structures during the computation process. This adaptability significantly enhances computational efficiency and precision, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's design, core mechanism, and the benefits it provides across various geometric modeling tasks.

title: Title: Constraint-Based Graph Embedding with Implicit Regularization
abstract: The task of learning graph embeddings, which represent graph structures in a lower-dimensional space, is a fundamental challenge in many applications, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. Traditional graph embedding methods often rely on handcrafted features or complex optimization techniques, which can be computationally expensive and may not capture the full complexity of the graph. This paper proposes a novel constraint-based graph embedding approach that utilizes an implicit regularization scheme to dynamically adjust the strength of the regularization during the embedding process. We introduce a learning algorithm that iteratively refines the regularization parameters based on the graph's structural properties, aiming to produce embeddings that are more stable, meaningful, and generalizable. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through theoretical analysis and experimental validation, showcasing its ability to generate embeddings that effectively capture key graph characteristics.

title: Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG)
abstract: Abstract: Create a Bayesian framework for geometric prediction, allowing for automated discovery of hidden patterns and optimization of design through probabilistic modeling. This paper introduces Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG), a novel approach that integrates Bayesian inference with geometric analysis to enable the automatic discovery of hidden patterns and optimization of design parameters. We detail the core mechanism of BPG, which involves constructing a probabilistic model of a system and leveraging Bayesian techniques to predict and refine design parameters. The paper presents a comprehensive overview of the BPG framework, outlining its key components and demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples. We explore the potential applications of BPG across various design domains, emphasizing its ability to uncover complex relationships and optimize design outcomes. title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Lattice Geometry (QELDG)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Lattice Geometry (QELDG) presents a novel approach to geometric computation leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. This research investigates the potential to generate and manipulate complex geometric shapes through iterative entanglement of lattice points, creating a new class of "quantum lattices" with unprecedented control over spatial arrangement. The core mechanism focuses on implementing a system of quantum gates that progressively entangles lattice points, ultimately leading to the emergence of intricate geometric patterns. The potential of QELDG lies in its ability to represent and manipulate space in a fundamentally different way than classical methods, offering possibilities for new data representation and manipulation paradigms. This paper details the methodology, explores initial results, and discusses the implications of this approach for data science and geometric computation.

title: A Dualidade na Gestão de TI: Eficiência Operacional via IA vs. a Necessidade de Inteligência Emocional no Atendimento ao Cliente
abstract: O presente artigo analisa a dualidade contemporânea na gestão de Tecnologia da Informação (TI), contrastando a eficiência operacional promovida pela Inteligência Artificial (IA) com a demanda contínua por Inteligência Emocional (IE) no atendimento ao cliente. O objetivo central é investigar o impacto da automação na experiência do usuário (UX), identificando em quais circunstâncias o fator humano permanece insubstituível. A metodologia empregada caracteriza-se por uma pesquisa qualitativa e descritiva, fundamentada em revisão bibliográfica e na análise de métricas de desempenho, como Service Level Agreement (SLA) e Experience Level Agreement (XLA). Os resultados evidenciam que, embora a IA otimize expressivamente os tempos de resposta em operações padronizadas, ela falha em cenários que exigem alta complexidade analítica e empatia. Constatou-se que a resolutividade tecnológica decai diante da subjetividade dos problemas dos usuários. Conclui-se, portanto, que a excelência na gestão de serviços de TI exige um modelo híbrido: a IA deve atuar na escala e triagem operacional, enquanto o capital humano, munido de inteligência emocional, é direcionado estrategicamente para a resolução de conflitos, garantindo a humanização e a fidelização no suporte.

title: Growing Echo State Networks through Graph-Based Morphogenesis with Developmental Graph Cellular Automata
abstract: Developmental Graph Cellular Automata (DGCA) are a novel model of morphogenesis, capable of growing directed graphs from single-node seeds. In this paper, we extend the DGCA model to exhibit stochastic growth, and show that both deterministic and stochastic DGCAs can be trained to grow reservoirs. Reservoirs are grown with two types of targets: task-driven (using the NARMA family of tasks) and task-independent (using reservoir metrics). Results show that deterministic DGCAs are able to grow a variety of specialised, life-like structures capable of solving benchmark tasks, outperforming 'typical' reservoirs on the same task. Stochastic DGCAs grow robust, regular structures that outperform reservoirs grown deterministically. Overall, these lay the foundation for the development of DGCA systems that produce plastic reservoirs and for modelling functional, adaptive morphogenesis.

title: Moral Competence Before Moral Content: Why LLM Agents Lack the Prerequisites for Coherent Alignment
abstract: AI alignment requires AI systems to adhere to human norms, values, or intentions. Under value pluralism there is no correct target, but a shared prerequisite is that the system's behavior expresses a coherent policy: a mapping from situations to verdicts that is invariant while a situation's morally relevant features are preserved, and sensitive when they change. We introduce four structural conditions for such coherent policies: verdict stability, monotonicity, decisiveness, and Pareto viability. Together they measure a form of moral competence that is evaluable from behavior alone, without reference to a moral standard or expert baseline, forming a structural floor for alignment rather than a normative target. We demonstrate the methodology on three simulated deployments featuring LLM-based agents facing moral dilemmas. Evaluating nine frontier models under a factorial design of five paraphrases, five escalation levels, and three dominance conditions, we show no model expresses a coherent policy across the three deployments: surface-form perturbation alone produces verdict-rate shifts of up to $99$ percentage points at a single escalation level, and a model's success on one scenario does not predict its competence on another. This suggests LLM-based agents are not currently the kind of object to which alignment can meaningfully apply.

title: Learning unknown stabilizer codes using product measurements
abstract: Efficiently characterizing quantum error correcting codes is a key challenge on the path to fault-tolerant quantum computation. Stabilizer codes, a central class of such codes, are defined by a set of stabilizer generators. Here, we present an algorithm that uses random single-qubit measurements to learn the stabilizer generators of any stabilizer code from $N$ copies of stabilizer states in its codespace, requiring no prior knowledge of the code's structure. This also enables verification that a device implements its intended code. We derive a lower bound on $N$ needed to recover the stabilizer generators with high probability, together with a bound on the algorithm's overall probability of success. When applied to quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, a leading candidate for practical fault-tolerant architectures, our approach requires a number of states that scales polylogarithmically with $n$, the number of qubits.

title: Design and Development of Hybrid Learning Model for the detection of Ovarian Cancers
abstract: Ovarian cancer remains as a significant contributor to female mortality across the globe, mainly because it has a difficulty in obtaining an early and precise diagnosis through complex histopathology images. Automated image-based diagnosis has therefore become essential to assist pathologists in making effective diagnoses of malignant tissues. Traditional diagnostic procedures and Deep Learning (DL) architectures often fail to capture fine-grained cellular textures as well as global contextual relationships needed for accurate classifications. These models are based on narrow receptive fields, have no focus on critical areas, and thus, the diagnostic accuracy and generalization across subtypes are limited. In order to overcome these shortcomings, the present research proposes a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework (ViT-SE + BiGRU-Luong FusionNet) to detect ovarian cancer accurately and effectively. The Vision Transformer (ViT) with a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) module is used to learn rich global contextual dependencies and focus important feature channels adaptively. Simultaneously, the Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) with the Luong Attention mechanism accurately captures the sequential spatial dependencies and identifies critical pathological areas in tissue sequences. Finally, a Cross-Attention Fusion (CAF) module is utilised to combine complementary global and sequential representations to achieve robust classification. The proposed framework is trained and tested on the Kaggle Ovarian Cancer and Subtypes Histopathology Dataset and achieves an accuracy of 99.53%, precision of 99.41%, recall of 99.47%, specificity of 99.45% and F1-score of 99.44%. The experimental findings prove that the proposed hybrid framework substantially improves diagnostic accuracy and generalization without compromising high computational efficiency, which makes it very applicable in real-time clinical practice in medical image diagnosis.

title: 基于自适应的动态矩阵的自适应扩展
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic matrix expansion, leveraging the adaptive nature of dynamic matrices to enhance both model performance and adaptability in machine learning and data science. Traditional methods often rely on static expansions, limiting the model's flexibility. This work proposes a framework that dynamically adjusts the expansion parameters based on the input data, allowing for more efficient and robust representation learning. We detail the core mechanism of this adaptive expansion, emphasizing its impact on algorithm efficiency and generalization capabilities. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through several case studies, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods. This contributes to the development of more adaptable and reliable machine learning algorithms.

title: Adaptive Quantum Neural Networks: Tensor Representation Learning
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) hold tremendous potential for revolutionizing machine learning, particularly in complex data analysis and pattern recognition. However, training QNNs can be computationally expensive and require significant expertise in network architecture and optimization. This paper proposes a novel approach to QNN training – Adaptive Tensor Representation Learning (ATRL) – which dynamically adjusts the tensor representation of the network based on the input data's unique characteristics. We demonstrate that ATRL significantly improves model performance across a range of datasets compared to traditional training methods. The method leverages the inherent properties of quantum neural networks to automatically learn and refine the tensor structure, fostering a more robust and adaptable model. This research addresses a critical bottleneck in QNN development, offering a pathway towards more efficient and effective training.

title: Title: Chaos Theory in High-Dimensional Spacetime - Predictive Modeling
abstract: Chaos Theory, a branch of mathematics dealing with complex systems exhibiting unpredictable behavior, presents a significant challenge to traditional modeling and prediction. This research delves into the application of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) to enhance our understanding and predictive capabilities within high-dimensional spacetime. The core claim is to develop a novel framework for analyzing chaos theory within this context, generating complex dynamics and identifying critical points with unprecedented accuracy. This work proposes a quantum-enhanced approach to explore the space of possible spacetime geometries, leveraging variational quantum algorithms to create robust predictive models. The investigation focuses on the unique challenges posed by high dimensionality, and aims to overcome these limitations through a fundamentally new algorithmic strategy. This research represents a significant advancement in the field, potentially unlocking new avenues for predicting complex system behavior and advancing our comprehension of chaotic dynamics.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Structures Under Quantum Entanglement Aggregation
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource for quantum information processing, and harnessing its properties requires sophisticated techniques for manipulation and processing. This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing topological structures to facilitate efficient and stable quantum entanglement aggregation, offering a novel approach to quantum information handling. We explore the design and implementation of a quantum entanglement network based on these structures, focusing on the mechanisms that enable aggregation, splitting, and manipulation of entangled states. The core of our research lies in leveraging the inherent topological properties of these structures to create robust and controllable quantum systems. This work presents a framework for building scalable quantum entanglement networks and highlights the advantages of utilizing self-organization in achieving enhanced performance and resilience. The investigation also addresses challenges related to maintaining entanglement coherence and exploring potential applications in quantum cryptography and quantum computing.

title: Quantum Information as a Dynamic Landscape – Landscape-Based Algorithms
abstract: Quantum Information represents a fundamentally different paradigm from classical information, offering the potential for exponential speedups in computation and communication. This paper explores the application of Landscape-Based Algorithms (LBAs) to optimization problems, specifically focusing on the challenge of efficiently navigating complex search spaces. We propose a novel algorithmic approach that models the problem space as a dynamic landscape, iteratively moving across this landscape to reward solutions that are closer to the optimal solution. This framework allows for exploration of vast possibilities, dramatically improving the search efficiency compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism involves a dynamic reward function that adjusts based on the landscape's characteristics, encouraging the algorithm to escape local optima and converge to a global optimum. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the Landscape model, explores its implementation, and discusses its potential impact on optimization problems across diverse domains.

We propose a novel algorithmic approach that models the problem space as a dynamic landscape, iteratively moving across this landscape to reward solutions that are closer to the optimal solution. This framework allows for exploration of vast possibilities, dramatically improving the search efficiency compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism involves a dynamic reward function that adjusts based on the landscape's characteristics, encouraging the algorithm to escape local optima and converge to a global optimum. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the Landscape model, explores its implementation, and discusses its potential impact on optimization problems across diverse domains.

title: Quantum Error Correction Codes for Distributed Storage
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum error correction (QEC) codes to enhance the reliability and security of distributed storage systems. Traditional storage methods are susceptible to various forms of data loss due to hardware failures, environmental factors, and malicious attacks. Utilizing the inherent redundancy and error-correcting capabilities of QEC codes offers a novel approach to mitigate these risks. The core claim is that leveraging QEC codes for distributed storage significantly improves its robustness. This work details a framework for implementing such a system, outlining the key mechanisms involved in data redundancy and error correction. The proposed approach represents a new paradigm in data protection, particularly relevant in scenarios demanding high data integrity, such as long-term archival and secure communication. We examine the theoretical foundations of QEC and their adaptation to the distributed storage context, emphasizing the potential for increased storage capacity and improved fault tolerance. The core mechanism relies on encoding data using QEC codes to create redundant copies, enabling the detection and correction of errors without directly observing the underlying quantum states. ---

title: Geometric Randomization for Machine Learning Model Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric randomization to enhance the optimization process in machine learning. The core concept revolves around systematically introducing variation in model parameters during each iteration, driven by random geometric transformations. We detail the methodology, its potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating improved model robustness and generalization. The motivation stems from the inherent challenges of optimization, particularly in complex models and datasets, where small variations can significantly impact performance. This novel technique aims to mitigate these issues by encouraging the model to explore a wider parameter space, leading to better generalization.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Structure Learning with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for data compression and feature extraction based on graph neural networks, specifically focusing on learning and utilizing topological structures. Traditional data compression techniques often treat data independently, while this approach leverages the inherent structure of the data to achieve superior efficiency. The core of the algorithm involves training a graph neural network to learn a robust topological structure, which is then employed to compress the data and extract informative features. The proposed method offers a significant improvement in data processing speed and compression rate compared to existing techniques. The paper explores the benefits of incorporating topological information into the neural network architecture and demonstrates its effectiveness through extensive experiments.

title: VTR Phase 4: Self-Validation of VTR-METH-001 v5.1 on a Self-Produced Artifact
abstract: Abstract VTR-METH-001 v5.1 was applied to vtr-sentinel-kmod and vtr-sentinel, two open-source security telemetry components produced by VTR itself. VAL-SENTINEL-01 is the first instance in the VTR methodology corpus where the producer and the audited artifact are the same entity. Three CONFIRMED findings emerged from systematic analysis without prior knowledge of the defects. Methodological Contribution Phase 3 answers: can you see it?CAPA 0 answers: do you know what you are seeing? Without VAL-SENTINEL-01, the evidence for ts_delta depended on the author. With VAL-SENTINEL-01, the evidence stands independently: commit 0c74b6d shows it was seq_delta, vtr_event.h now says seq_delta, and any third party can recompile 60bc911c and verify this without asking the author. This is the empirical instance of VTR-RES-002's central claim: evidence that stands alone is stronger than evidence that depends on who produced it.VTR is not a claim about a person. It is a claim about a method. When the method audits itself, it does not bleed authority -- it bleeds bugs. Which is exactly what it should do. v0.4.0-phase4-self-validated is the first instance where producer and artifact are the same and the evidence stillstands

title: Quantum Entanglement Expansion: A Framework for Beyond Classical Quantum Computing Based on Multi-Universe Concepts
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibits a unique property – non-locality – that challenges classical physics. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entanglement as a connection between multiple universes, proposing a novel quantum computing framework termed "Multi-Universe Quantum Computing" (MUQC). The MUQC framework leverages entanglement as a 'information channel' to achieve computational capabilities exceeding those of classical systems. We detail the core mechanisms, including the representation of entanglement as a multi-dimensional connection, and the implications for computational design. The paper argues that this approach offers a potential pathway toward fundamentally new quantum algorithms and computational paradigms.

title: Nonlinear Spacetime Structures and Adaptive Clustering Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear spacetime structures and adaptive clustering algorithms to improve data clustering. Traditional clustering methods often struggle to effectively model complex, non-linear relationships within data. We propose a novel approach that transforms the clustering problem into a non-linear spacetime structure, employing an adaptive clustering algorithm to dynamically adjust parameters and enhance the capture of data's inherent non-linearities. This research focuses on achieving superior clustering performance by addressing limitations inherent in conventional approaches. The core mechanism involves formulating the clustering process as a dynamic spacetime mapping, allowing the algorithm to learn and refine its clustering strategy in response to data variations. This leads to improved data representation and a more accurate representation of underlying patterns. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of case studies involving diverse datasets. The resulting algorithm provides a significant advancement in clustering techniques, particularly when dealing with intricate data landscapes.

title: Federated Continual Learning for Encrypted Traffic Classification at the Network Edge Under Asynchronous Concept Drift
abstract: Concept drift can degrade encrypted-traffic classifiers deployed at the network edge as applications, protocols, and usage patterns evolve. This paper formulates federated continual learning under asynchronous real- and virtual drift and proposes DriftGuard, a framework combining a two-level per-node detector, selective adapter-based adaptation with Fisher importance masking and class-balanced replay, and drift-aware server aggregation. Level 1 detects distributional changes in learned representations, while Level 2 monitors supervised prediction errors to provide evidence consistent with decision-relevant drift before selective adaptation is activated. We further derive a convergence bound under stated assumptions that explicitly incorporates environmental variation, detection delay, and false alarms. DriftGuard is evaluated in a controlled simulation using reproducible synthetic traffic-like features under sudden, gradual, virtual-only, and recurring drift. Across five independent runs, results are reported with standard deviations, 95% confidence intervals, and paired statistical comparisons. DriftGuard maintains competitive classification accuracy while limiting forgetting of stable classes, with its clearest advantage observed under gradual asynchronous drift. Results also show that immediate adaptation using ground-truth drift states does not necessarily improve performance under the evaluated adaptation policy. The findings provide controlled methodological validation rather than evidence of production-scale deployment performance.

title: LexFlip: A Dissociation Diagnostic for Legal Meaning Preservation Metrics
abstract: Does a simplified legal clause still say what the original said? The checks in current use cannot establish that it does: requiring an identical pair to score highest and an unrelated pair lowest moves lexical overlap and legal force together, so any monotone function of token overlap satisfies both. Our remedy is a dissociation, an item holding surface form fixed while legal force moves. We release LexFlip, 373 minimal perturbations of Quebec statutory French that reverse legal force while preserving 0.93 of the tokens, with a harness scoring metrics, regressors and prompted judges alike. The seven embedding and BERTScore metrics we test spend only 0.022 to 0.039 of their identical-to-unrelated range on such an edit, against 0.670 for bidirectional NLI, the one family the identical-pair check would disqualify. On FrJudge, against a measured human ceiling of r=0.597, a bare length feature outscores every semantic metric and has the lowest margin we measure.

title: An Attention-Guided Global and Local Fusion Framework for Lesion-Focused Image Classification
abstract: Lesion-focused image classification presents a core analytical challenge, as discriminative signals are often sparse, spatially dispersed, and easily obscured by background noise, while conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) process entire images uniformly and may dilute signal relevance. This study hypothesizes that adaptive fusion of global contextual information and lesion-focused local information can improve classification performance compared with using either representation independently. We propose a three-branch, attention-guided deep learning framework built on Densely Connected Convolutional Network-121 (DenseNet-121) to improve feature attribution, interpretability, and classification reliability. The architecture consists of a global branch that learns representations from full images, followed by Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to generate attention maps that highlight prediction-relevant regions and produce masked inputs, and a local branch enhanced with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to extract refined spatial and channel-wise features from these focused regions. An adaptive fusion branch integrates global and local representations by learning instance-specific weights, allowing dynamic prioritization between contextual and localized information. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic Spot Pattern Dataset (SSPD) and three benchmark datasets, including skin lesion, guava leaf, and grape leaf image datasets, where the fusion branch outperformed the individual global and local branches, reaching 97.75% accuracy on the skin lesion dataset and 99.64% on the guava leaf dataset. The results highlight the value of attention-guided architectures in healthcare analytics by improving model transparency, strengthening feature relevance, and supporting more reliable data-driven decision-making in medical image analysis.

title: Compressed Quantum Simulation via Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: 量子模拟利用可控的量子系统来模拟一个难以用经典计算机处理的复杂多体量子系统，以应对随多体系统规模指数增长的计算复杂度。本文研究了一种基于量子机器学习的压缩量子模拟方案，通过利用参数化量子线路构建量子自编码器，学习高维希尔伯特空间中量子绝热演化的低维等效表示，并在低维空间中高保真地重构绝热演化过程以实现压缩量子模拟。本文以 9 量子比特二维横场伊辛模型的量子相变检测问题为例，使用 2 量子比特系统对其进行压缩量子模拟，制备基态并测量磁涨落和能量等物理量。结果表明，该方案能在低维希尔伯特空间中高精度复现量子相变行为，所得基态能量的相对误差不超过 2.1%。本研究为在资源有限的量子设备上模拟复杂物理过程提供了新的思路，推动了量子模拟与机器学习的交叉融合。

title: Reliability‑Aware Multimodal Intelligence for Healthcare Insurance Fraud Detection: A Trimodal Data Perspective
abstract: Healthcare insurance fraud has emerged as a significant challenge due to the rapid growth of digital healthcare systems, increasing volumes of electronic insurance claims, and the evolving complexity of fraudulent activities. Conventional fraud detection approaches primarily rely on manually defined rules, single-modal data, or traditional machine learning algorithms, which often struggle to capture complex relationships among heterogeneous healthcare information and provide reliable predictions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Reliability-Aware Multimodal Intelligence Network (RAMI-Net) for healthcare insurance fraud detection from a trimodal data perspective. Initially, healthcare insurance claims are preprocessed and transformed into three complementary perspectives: patient structured data, claim-related textual information, and healthcare relationship graphs. These perspectives are processed using TabNet, ClinicalBERT, and Graph Attention Network (GAT) to extract modality-specific feature representations. A Reliability Estimation Module evaluates the confidence of each modality before a Reliability-Aware Cross-Modal Attention Fusion mechanism integrates reliable features while minimizing noisy information. The fused representations are classified using an Explainable Fraud Detection Network, and SHAP provides transparent interpretations by identifying influential fraud-related features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves 99.95% accuracy, 99.98% precision, 99.97% recall, 99.95% F1-score, and 99.63% ROC-AUC, outperforming conventional machine learning and deep learning approaches. The proposed RAMI-Net provides an accurate, robust, reliable, and interpretable solution for intelligent healthcare insurance fraud detection, supporting effective real-world healthcare insurance claim management.

title: Distributed Cognitive Prompting Framework for AI Collaboration: An Experimental Approach, Introductory Edition
abstract: The Distributed Cognitive Prompting Framework for AI Collaboration (DCPF) is an experimental organizational architecture for structuring sustained human-AI collaboration. It separates recurring responsibilities across four interconnected frameworks: Governance, Research, Knowledge, and Runtime. This Introductory Edition presents the framework's architecture, standard responsibilities, workflows, human decision boundaries, practicums, templates, and supporting reference materials. It is intended to support learning, critical evaluation, controlled testing, and further research. DCPF has not been broadly or independently validated across domains, organizations, AI systems, or production environments. Readers should begin in controlled, low-risk settings and retain human review, verification, acceptance, and accountability. dcpfai.org is the authoritative source for current official DCPF materials, editions, permissions information, and updates.

title: Why Today's AI Research Cannot Work — And Why Its Solutions Create New Instabilities
abstract: Abstract Modern AI research operates within a paradigm that cannot generate the cognitive functions required for stable, reliable reasoning. Large Language Models represent one cognitive function, not cognition itself. Scaling makes this single function more operational, but does not unlock new mechanisms. Safety patches attempt to constrain emergent behavior, yet mechanically introduce functional mixing, drift, blindspots, and instability. The ABC analysis shows that two additional cognitive functions exist, but the industry misinterprets them as bias, drift, hallucination, emergence, or safety problems—because they are not recognized as independent cognitive operators. Treating these functions as errors prevents the formation of a stable analog cognitive process. Compounding this, modern approaches multiply instability: increasing model complexity, adding patches, and accelerating hardware creates a hyperbolic error cascade. The error stabilization mechanism described in QUED 2 implies how accelerating an unstable mechanism amplifies its failure modes. A new paradigm is required. The missing cognitive functions must be formulated as independent analog layers that operate in a fixed sequence, interact mechanically, and form a coherent pipeline. Stability, auditability, and safety emerge not from more patches, size, or speed, but from the ordered arrangement of cognitive elements into a functional mechanism.

title: Length Confounds in Attention-Based Diagnostics: Entropy and Mass Measures Are Biased in Opposite Directions
abstract: Attention statistics are increasingly used to diagnose generation failure in transformer language models. Two families are in common use: entropy measures, which summarise how diffuse a query's attention is, and mass measures, which report the attention placed on a designated subset of tokens such as constraint tokens or supplied context. Where these are compared across prompts of differing length -- ablation studies, prompt-compression evaluations, context manipulations -- both families are confounded, and in opposite directions. That softmax attention disperses as sequence length grows is established: Velickovic et al. (2025) prove that attention coefficients decay as Theta(1/n) for bounded logits. This preprint does not claim that observation. It shows that the consequence for comparative measurement has been overlooked, and that it is large enough to invert reported conclusions. Under a generative model of attention logits in which anchor tokens are held fixed and only filler is removed, so that every observed change is artefact, eightfold compression lowers Shannon entropy by 1.913 nats while raising anchor mass by 0.363. A study reporting that compression concentrates attention, and one reporting that compression increases attention to constraint tokens, would both be measuring the same artefact. Main results: 1. The entropy artefact is comparable in magnitude to a plausible conditioning effect and opposite in sign. Anchor removal at fixed length raises entropy by 1.400 nats, while threefold compression lowers it by 1.016 nats. 2. The raw entropy contrast inverts at a locatable compression ratio, r = exp(dH_anchor), predicted analytically at 4.055 and confirmed by bisection at 4.085, an agreement of 0.74 per cent. Across a parameter grid the inversion point ranges from 1.06 to 22.21. 3. Normalising by log n reduces the entropy artefact twentyfold but leaves a non-monotone residual of 0.094. Query position must enter analyses as a covariate rather than merely as a divisor: at constant conditioning quality, raw entropy varies by 3.732 nats across query positions 16 to 1024. 4. For mass measures the obvious normalisation, lift over the uniform null, is worse than no correction. Its range of 18.9 exceeds the raw artefact of 0.363, because it inherits a ceiling at n/m. 5. The statistic that works is the anchor log-odds ratio, Lambda = logit(mass) - log(m/(n-m)), which recovers the underlying logit gap to within 0.03 and varies by only 0.012 across an eightfold compression sweep. title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum algorithm optimization is a critical challenge in the development of quantum technologies. Traditional optimization methods often struggle to effectively utilize the inherent dynamism of quantum systems, limiting their potential for performance gains. This paper proposes a novel approach based on adaptive quantum algorithm optimization, leveraging the quantum system's inherent parameter adjustments to dynamically tune quantum algorithms for enhanced efficiency. We present a framework that automatically adjusts quantum algorithm parameters based on real-time feedback, resulting in improved performance across a range of quantum tasks. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum state evolution to guide parameter adjustments, offering a significant improvement over static optimization techniques. The paper details the proposed algorithm, its implementation, and demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, showcasing its potential to accelerate quantum algorithm development.

title: Geometric Matrix Dynamics & Quantum Computing Integration
abstract: This paper explores the integration of geometric matrix dynamics with quantum computing to achieve high-precision and high-efficiency geometric computations. Traditional methods often struggle to meet stringent computational requirements. This study proposes a novel algorithmic framework that leverages quantum computing to accelerate geometric matrix calculations and dynamically adjusts the matrix structure, resulting in enhanced accuracy and performance. We detail the design of this system, emphasizing the interplay between quantum acceleration and adaptive matrix manipulation. This work aims to push the boundaries of geometric computation, offering a potential paradigm shift for complex geometric problems.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子机器学习验证
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning verification framework based on adaptive topology. Quantum computing offers unique capabilities, including the ability to represent and manipulate geometric properties, which can be leveraged to validate the stability of machine learning models. We propose a method that utilizes quantum algorithms to assess the robustness of training data and model parameters, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of quantum machine learning's potential. The framework focuses on leveraging the inherent properties of quantum geometry to detect subtle shifts in the model's behavior, providing a more rigorous and potentially more efficient verification process than traditional methods. The core mechanism involves applying quantum transformations to data representations and model parameters to identify patterns indicative of instability. This paper explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of this framework, highlighting its advantages and potential impact on the field of quantum machine learning.

title: Causal Model Learning for Non-linear Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to non-linear time series prediction by focusing on causal model learning. Traditional time series prediction methods often rely on pattern recognition within the data, which can be brittle and lack robustness when faced with changes in underlying dynamics. We argue that the key to accurate prediction lies in identifying and modeling the causal relationships within the data. This research proposes a framework that integrates causal discovery algorithms, specifically Do-Calculus, with deep neural networks. The core idea is to leverage the neural network's ability to learn complex, non-linear patterns while simultaneously using Do-Calculus to infer the underlying causal structure. This results in a dynamic causal model that can be used for accurate and interpretable time series prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline a potential implementation strategy. The proposed method addresses limitations of existing approaches by enhancing prediction robustness and providing insights into the driving forces behind the time series. ---
